state.lastRunNotes: Reviewed AAPL, GOOGL, META (all held, no fresh catalysts beyond their existing multi-week theses) plus the day's big movers (INTC, AMD, CRM). Real-world news confirms INTC/AMD momentum is a continuation of the Meta Muse AI-driven CPU-demand narrative and CRM's rally is a month-long AI/Agentforce re-rating -- both already priced in, with no unusual volume today (vol_x well under 1.5x), so not fresh, tradable catalysts. ADBE's drop is stale post-earnings/CEO-transition weakness, not a dip worth buying. Rising long yields are pressuring staples/retail/financials broadly (COST, HD, PEP, JPM, XLF) but that's macro rotation, not a stock-specific catalyst. Growth/core split is 61%/39% (within the 35-65% band, no genuine catalyst to rebalance). Holding everything, no day-trades since this is the last session of the day.

trades.horizon: Medium-term (~2-4 months) — through the iPhone Duo launch cycle and holiday-quarter earnings
trades.rationale: Apple unveiled the $1,999 foldable iPhone Duo, its biggest hardware redesign in years; Citi reiterated Buy with a $365 target and called it Apple's most significant new hardware category since the Watch/AirPods.
trades.sentimentSummary: Analyst commentary strongly bullish on the Duo launch; stock rallying even as broader tech sells off.

trades.horizon: Medium-term (~1-3 months) — tracking Muse AI adoption/monetization signals into next earnings
trades.rationale: Meta's Muse AI agent (task-completing assistant, #3 in App Store) is driving a fresh bull case beyond ads; JPMorgan upgraded to Buy ($820 PT) and Goldman reaffirmed Buy after the launch.
trades.sentimentSummary: Wall Street broadly bullish post-Muse launch, with some debate over monetization risk longer term.

trades.horizon: Short-to-medium-term (4-8 weeks) — reassess into Alphabet's Oct 27, 2026 Q3 earnings as the post-ruling rally digests and DOJ appeal risk is monitored.
trades.rationale: A federal judge's antitrust remedy ruling lets Google keep Chrome and avoids a forced breakup, removing a years-long regulatory overhang; shares are up sharply post-ruling with a Strong Buy analyst consensus (~$428 avg PT, 58 buys/0 sells) and bullish chatter calling it a breakout to fresh highs.
trades.sentimentSummary: Broadly bullish across financial media and retail trader chatter (TradingView/Reddit-adjacent) framing the ruling as a major overhang removed; Jim Cramer called it a 'shockingly favorable' outcome.
